subject: Capacity preflight: Dedicated GPU sizing & standby plan for OptiLabs
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Shaw <emma.shaw@optilabs.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity preflight: Dedicated GPU sizing & standby plan for OptiLabs

Emma / team — following our exec alignment yesterday, OptiLabs looks set to move from PoC to an initial Dedicated commitment. Before we finalize the commercial terms, we need a short internal preflight to validate the GPU sizing and a small standby hold for the closing window (two-week ramp).

Ask: can infra confirm a recommended dedicated pool profile and a conservative standby allocation we can pledge for the first 90 days? Key constraints / inputs:
- Expected steady-state: 8 concurrent instances at 2k tokens/session average latency target 150–250ms p50 for gen workloads.
- Peak expected burst: ~3x steady-state for 2–3 hours/day.
- Model: optilabs will run a mix of Llama-3-22B fine-tuned and a smaller 7B reranker.

We'd like a simple runbook for the customer-facing commit: instance sizing, quantization option we recommend, fallback variant for capacity shortfalls, and an explicit standby count (N GPUs) we can advertise in the contract. Attached: draft MOA and their sizing worksheet from OptiLabs.

Target: internal sign-off on numbers by EOD Wednesday so we can bake the hold into the contract (they want a soft start date of 2028-08-01).

Thanks — Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Director, Strategic Deals | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Emma Shaw <emma.shaw@optilabs.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity preflight: Dedicated GPU sizing & standby plan for OptiLabs

Thanks Laura — I dug into run rates and put a sizing recommendation into the attached runbook (dedicated-runbook-v1.xlsx). Short summary here:
- Base config: 8 production pods, each backed by 1x A100 80GB (or 1x H100-80 where available) with 4GB KV cache per pod. This covers the 2k token median with headroom for batching and caching.
- Burst plan: autoscaler policy to allow +16 GPUs (2x headroom) for 2-hour bursts.
- Standby hold recommendation: reserve 4 GPUs (A100 80GB equiv) for the two-week ramp window and first 30 days as a safety buffer. This is large enough to absorb 20–30% above forecast without impacting other customers.
- Quantization: enable FP16 + 4-bit activation paths for the 22B model to cut token cost ~35% while keeping latency within p50 targets.
- Fallback: a trimmed 13B variant with identical prompt interfaces; automated routing if queued latency crosses 600ms p95.

I've also stubbed a short escalation play (“If reserved pool > 70% utilized then notify capacity@redwood and enact burst policy”) and added suggested wording we can drop in the MOA for the standby hold (soft hold with 14-day notice).

Attaching runbook and a short SLA options PDF for OptiLabs to review.

Ben

Subject: Re: Capacity preflight: Dedicated GPU sizing & standby plan for OptiLabs

Laura / Ben — thanks for the quick turnaround and the spreadsheet. A few clarifying questions from OptiLabs:
1) Can you confirm whether the standby hold of 4 GPUs would incur full committed billing or a lower standby rate? Our procurement team flagged price delta for reserved-but-idle GPUs.
2) If we ship with the 22B quantized path, what regression monitoring do you provide so we can track quality vs. the unquantized baseline?

Procurement (cc) — we need to confirm billing for standby in the MOA. Ideally a reduced standby fee or credit applied if not consumed after 90 days.

Emma

emma.shaw@optilabs.ai

Date: Tue, 17 Jul 2028 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity preflight: Dedicated GPU sizing & standby plan for OptiLabs

Emma — quick answers from commercial side and next steps:
- Standby billing: we can offer a reduced standby rate (typically 30% of committed GPU rate) for the first 90 days; after 90 days it converts to normal committed billing unless used/consumed. I'll have procurement language drafted for MOA.
- Regression monitoring: Redwood Optimize will run the evaluation hooks you include (we’ll ingest your eval set) and report quality deltas. We can add a regression alert tied to your golden prompt set; option to gate quantized rollout if delta > 2% on your key metrics.

Action items:
- Monica, please help convert Ben's runbook numbers into the MOA clause for standby rate and the soft-hold terms.
- Rishi, can you validate we have 4 GPUs free in the SFO-dedicated pool for 2028-08-01 start (or equivalent in us-west region)? If the pool is tight, propose an alternate standby location and ETA for migration.

I'll draft the MOA language and circulate for sign-off by EOD Wednesday.

Thanks — Karthik

--

Quick status update & confirmed items for the thread:
- Rishi confirmed pool availability: 4 A100-80GB equivalents are available in SFO on 2028-08-01. If demand spikes in week 2, we can shift 2 GPUs from us-west-2 warm pool within 6 hours.
- I've drafted standby billing clause: 30% standby fee for first 90 days; 30-day notice to release, and prorated credits if OptiLabs consumes standby capacity within the 90-day window. (See attached MOA PDF for redline).
- Ben's runbook accepted; added a small sentence requiring Redwood Optimize eval hooks be turned on during the first 14 days.

Next steps: Laura to push MOA to OptiLabs legal with the updated clause; Karthik to confirm DocuSign link and procurement cadence.
